images.title: Same ending, different answer
images.purpose: Show that 108 and 208 share the last two digits 08, yet 208 is a multiple of 8 and 108 is not, so two digits cannot decide divisibility by 8.
images.composition: Two number rows stacked with wide space between them, each with a small result line to its right, centred on a white page.
images.exact_structure: Top row: three equal boxes holding 1, 0, 8; the last two boxes filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Bottom row: three equal boxes holding 2, 0, 8; the last two boxes filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Right of the top row, one grey #6B7280 line of text. Right of the bottom row, one teal #0072B2 line of text. Exactly 2 rows, 6 boxes, 2 result lines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
rows of different box sizes, or more than 2 rows
images.takeaway: The same last two digits can give different answers for 8.
images.description: Two rows of digit boxes, 108 and 208, both ending in 08 highlighted; 208 = 8 × 26 while 108 is not a multiple.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to compare the two highlighted endings and say what is different about the numbers.

image_decisions.why: Two numbers with the same ending but different results show the point at a glance; one clean image carries it.
